title: Bifibrant comparison for enriched localization inside a chunk
statement:
Use combinatorial simplicial model categories, their cofibrant and fibrant objects, and weak equivalences as in [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], and enriched localization and Dwyer--Kan equivalences as in [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus]. Fix sufficiently large universes. Let $\mathcal A$ be a combinatorial simplicial model category and $U\subseteq\mathcal A$ a small full simplicial subcategory satisfying the following chunk closure conditions, with choices functorial by simplicially enriched functors. For every finite fan $X\to Y_i$ in $U$, the product map factors as a trivial cofibration $X\to Z$ followed by a fibration $Z\to\prod_iY_i$ with $Z\in U$; for every finite cofan $Y_i\to X$ in $U$, the coproduct map factors as a cofibration $\coprod_iY_i\to Z$ followed by a trivial fibration $Z\to X$ with $Z\in U$. Empty families are included. Write $U^f=U\cap\mathcal A^f$, $U^{cf}=U\cap\mathcal A^{cf}$, and let $W$ be the model weak equivalences between objects of $U^f$. Inclusion followed by enriched localization induces a Dwyer--Kan equivalence
$$\eta_U:U^{cf}\longrightarrow U^f[W^{-1}].$$
This is the comparison using the actual enriched mapping simplicial sets. For a simplicial functor $F:U\to U'$ between such chunks in possibly different combinatorial simplicial model categories, if $F$ carries fibrant objects, bifibrant objects and weak equivalences to objects and arrows of the corresponding kind, the square of $\eta_U,\eta_{U'}$ with the restrictions of $F$ and its induced localization map commutes.

source.place: Lemma A.3.6.17, printed p.904, specialized to simplicial sets; naturality of inclusion followed by localization Read online on 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopy-theoretic assertion.

proof.text: Apply the assumed enriched functorial cofan factorization to the empty cofan at each $X\in U$. It gives $\varnothing\to QX\xrightarrow{q_X}X$, with $QX\in U$, the first arrow a cofibration and $q_X$ a trivial fibration. The stated enriched functoriality supplies a simplicial functor $Q:U\to U$ and an enriched natural transformation $q:Q\to1_U$. If $X$ is fibrant, composition of $q_X$ with $X\to *$ is a fibration, so $QX$ is bifibrant. Naturality gives $q_YQ(f)=fq_X$, so two-out-of-three shows that $Q$ carries weak equivalences to weak equivalences. Consequently inclusion $i:U^{cf}\to U^f$ and $Q:U^f\to U^{cf}$ preserve the specified weak equivalences. Their transformations $iQ\to1_{U^f}$ and $Qi\to1_{U^{cf}}$ have weak-equivalence components.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.3.6.17, printed p.904 (PDF p.922), interval argument; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-enriched assertion.

proof.text: Put $G=W\cap\operatorname{Ar}(U^{cf})$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be in $G$. Apply the one-fan factorization in the chunk to $f$ to obtain $X\xrightarrow{i_f}Z\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$ with $i_f$ a trivial cofibration and $p_f$ a fibration. Two-out-of-three makes $p_f$ trivial; $Z$ is cofibrant because $X$ is, and fibrant because $Y$ is. Lifting against $X\to *$ gives $r:Z\to X$ with $ri_f=1_X$. Lifting against $\varnothing\to Y$ gives $s:Y\to Z$ with $p_fs=1_Y$. Thus all objects and all vertex arrows used in the following calculation lie in the full subcategory $U^{cf}$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.3.6.17, printed p.904 (PDF p.922), interval argument; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-enriched assertion.

proof.text: The simplicial model axiom gives trivial Kan fibrations $i_f^*:\operatorname{Map}(Z,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(X,Z)$ and $(p_f)_*:\operatorname{Map}(Z,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(Z,Y)$. For the first use the trivial cofibration $i_f$ and the fibration $Z\to *$; for the second use the cofibration $\varnothing\to Z$ and the trivial fibration $p_f$. The vertices $i_fr$ and $1_Z$ have the same image $i_f$ in the first map; $sp_f$ and $1_Z$ have the same image $p_f$ in the second. Lifting $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ over these constant edges joins the respective pairs. Hence $[i_fr]=[1_Z]=[sp_f]$ in the component category. It follows that $[rs][f]=[r][sp_f][i_f]=1_X$ and $[f][rs]=[p_f][i_fr][s]=1_Y$. Every arrow of $G$ is therefore invertible in $\pi_0U^{cf}$, using the actual enriched mapping simplicial sets.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.3.6.17, printed p.904 (PDF p.922), interval argument; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-enriched assertion.

proof.text: The localization-at-already-invertible-arrows clause of [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus] now gives a Dwyer--Kan equivalence $a:U^{cf}\to L_GU^{cf}$. The relative enriched functors $i,Q$ from step 1 induce $\bar i:L_GU^{cf}\to L_WU^f$ and $\bar Q:L_WU^f\to L_GU^{cf}$ by functoriality of enriched localization. Notice that this uses the localization-at-equivalences clause only; the comparison for an entire model category is not being applied to the chunk, which need not itself be a model category.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.3.6.17, printed p.904 (PDF p.922), interval argument; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-enriched assertion.

proof.text: Let $\ell:U^f\to L_WU^f$ and $a:U^{cf}\to L_GU^{cf}$ be the structure maps of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. Functoriality of localization (step 4) gives $\bar ia=\ell i$ and $\bar Q\ell=aQ$, and induced maps are compatible with composition in $h\mathrm{sCat}$; hence $[\ell iQ]=[\bar i][\bar Q][\ell]$ and $[aQi]=[\bar Q][\bar i][a]$. Since $\ell$ is a simplicial functor, whiskering the enriched transformation $q:iQ\to1_{U^f}$ of step 1 gives an enriched natural transformation $\ell q:\ell iQ\to\ell$: the two composition maps agree after applying $\ell$ on mapping simplicial sets. Its components $\ell(q_X)$ have $q_X\in W$, so they are isomorphisms in $\pi_0L_WU^f$: the class $[\ell]=\ell^*(1)$ lies in the image described in [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. [lem-coef-simplicial-natural-equivalence-homotopy] gives $[\ell iQ]=[\ell]$, and injectivity of $\ell^*$ on $\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(L_WU^f,L_WU^f)$ gives $[\bar i][\bar Q]=1$. The same argument with $a$, $G$ and $q:Qi\to1_{U^{cf}}$, whose components $q_X$ for bifibrant $X$ lie in $G$, gives $[\bar Q][\bar i]=1$. Thus $[\bar i]$ is an isomorphism in $h\mathrm{sCat}$, the model homotopy category of the Dwyer--Kan model structure. Apply [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] to that model category and its homotopy localization, as supplied by [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. It follows that $\bar i$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. The composite $\bar ia=\ell i$ is inclusion $U^{cf}\to U^f$ followed by localization, which is $\eta_U$, so two-out-of-three with step 4 proves the claimed comparison.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.3.6.17, printed p.904 (PDF p.922), interval argument; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-enriched assertion.

proof.text: For the simplicial functor $F:U\to U\prime$ in the statement, its restrictions $F^{cf}:U^{cf}\to U\prime^{cf}$ and $F^f:U^f\to U\prime^f$ exist by the two object-preservation hypotheses, and $F^f$ preserves the marked arrows by the weak-equivalence hypothesis. Write $\ell_U:U^f\to L_WU^f$ for localization and $i_U:U^{cf}\to U^f$ for inclusion. Functoriality gives $L(F^f)\ell_U=\ell_{U\prime}F^f$, and the restrictions satisfy $F^fi_U=i_{U\prime}F^{cf}$. Therefore $L(F^f)\eta_U=L(F^f)\ell_Ui_U=\ell_{U\prime}F^fi_U=\ell_{U\prime}i_{U\prime}F^{cf}=\eta_{U\prime}F^{cf}$. This is a commuting square for functorial localization choices and a commuting square in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ independently of those choices. No compatibility of $F$ with $Q$ is needed.

Step 2: the one-fan gives Z with both lifts r and s valid. Step 3: SM7 gives trivial Kan fibrations i_f^* and (p_f)_*, using Map(X,*)=* and Map(empty,-)=*; boundary lifting for Delta^1 is in kan-quillen; both inverse products check. Step 4: the already-invertible clause applies, and i and Q carry the markings correctly. Step 6: the naturality chain is correct. The new node lem-coef-enriched-natural-localization-homotopy is true (tested on [0] to [1] with W the arrow, on empty C and on W empty). But it is a few-line consequence of the existing same-unit node lem-coef-simplicial-natural-equivalence-homotopy plus the injectivity and image clause of lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property (C5/C1). The report did not compare it with that node or with simplicial-marked-cylinder-comparison. FIX: dropped the new node and rewrote step 5. It now whiskers q by the localization maps ell and a, gets [ell iQ]=[ell] and [aQi]=[a] from natural-equivalence-homotopy, and cancels ell and a by injectivity, giving [i-bar][Q-bar]=1 and [Q-bar][i-bar]=1.
